claims.claim: floating leaves are short-lived, 38–48 days on average in European lilies
claims.source_value: mean leaf life span 37.93–47.73 d across six plots (Nuphar lutea 42.75, 37.93, 47.73; Nymphaea alba 40.46, 46.46; Nymphaea candida 46.28); SD 13–20 d; maxima 73–92 d, minima 7–12 d
claims.location: web page (PeerJ article), Table 2 'Leaf characteristics', row 'Leaf life span — Mean'
claims.conditions: three Dutch water bodies (eutrophic Haarsteegse Wiel and Oude Waal, 1977; oligotrophic acid Voorste Goorven, 1988); one 1-m² plot per species and site in dense mono-specific stands; every floating leaf tagged and followed weekly; life span = time a leaf was at the surface (until its lamina detached, or sank at VG)

claims.claim: lily blades 51–215 (Nuphar) and 139–183 (Nymphaea) g AFDW m⁻² (Europe)
claims.source_value: maximum POTENTIAL floating-leaf-blade biomass: Nuphar lutea 215 (HW), 118 (OW), 51 (VG); Nymphaea alba 183 (OW), 139 (VG); Nymphaea candida 71 g AFDW m⁻²
claims.location: web page (PeerJ article), Table 2, row 'Leaf biomass — Max. pot.'
claims.conditions: seasonal maximum of floating blades only (no petioles or rhizomes), computed from leaf lengths with length–biomass regressions as the intact-leaf ('potential') biomass; same plots and years as above
claims.note: These are potential (intact) maxima; the actual maxima after leaf loss are 178/95/49 (Nuphar) and 153/136 (N. alba), and the green 'photosynthetic' maxima 155/74/43 and 135/133. The species are the European N. lutea and N. alba, not N. variegata or N. odorata; the table's '(Europe)' says so but the cell should say 'maximum potential blade biomass'. N. candida (71) is left out of the cell.
